## Natural history notes

A small jumping spider characterized by a compact body, large forward-facing eyes, and brown to grayish coloration with pale markings that help it blend against bark, leaves, and stems. In Florida, the Sylvan Jumping Spider is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, pine flatwoods, parks, gardens, and shrubs where it hunts on vegetation and tree trunks. It is an active daytime predator, stalking and pouncing on small insects and other arthropods with the aid of sharp vision, while using silk mainly for draglines, shelters, and egg sacs rather than prey capture.
